settings.text:
Awaken in the Valley of the Ancients

Journey with Gregg Braden through Monument Valley’s sacred landscapes for 10 days of wisdom, healing, and profound self-discovery.

Join Gregg Braden on an intimate retreat through the awe-inspiring beauty of Monument Valley, April 13–22, 2026. Located within the Navajo Nation, this 10-day journey invites you to walk among towering sandstone buttes, explore ancient petroglyphs, and connect with stories carried through generations. Guided by local Navajo people and grounded in spiritual practice, this immersive experience invites deep listening, personal growth, and sacred connection to the land.

This is no ordinary trip. It’s a Monument Valley tour unlike any other, woven with ceremony, science, and soul.

Guided by Gregg’s Pure Human: Breakthrough! teachings and the wisdom of indigenous Navajo guides, each day weaves immersive excursions with meditations and practices designed to unlock your highest potential. You’ll visit Mystery Valley, The Mittens, and the Three Sisters—embracing the spiritual resonance of this sacred land.

You’ll journey through the Tear Drop Arch, witness the powerful stillness of Valley of the Gods, and gather around the fire for Navajo stories, songs, and dark-sky celebration. You may even witness the legendary Ear of the Wind, one of Monument Valley’s most iconic rock formations.

This experience is more than a tour—it’s a living activation of self-discovery and connection with Gaia, Mother Earth, or Nihimá Nahasdzáán, as the Navajo call her.

Group size is limited to preserve intimacy and community. As you reflect in a Navajo hogan or meditate beneath towering cliffs, the shifting desert sky becomes your mirror. You’ll return to your essence—and remember the wisdom within.

✨ Reserve your place today for this unforgettable Gregg Braden tour through sacred Navajo lands.

settings.title: Gregg Braden
settings.text:
Gregg Braden is a five-time New York Times best-selling author, scientist, and a pioneer in the emerging paradigm bridging science, social policy, and human potential.

His research resulted in the 2003 discovery of intelligent information encoded into the human genome and the 2010 application of fractal time to predict future occurrences of past events. Gregg’s work has led to 15 film credits, 12 award-winning books now published in over 40 languages, and he was a 2020 nominee for the prestigious Templeton Prize. He has presented his discoveries in over 34 countries on six continents, and has been invited to speak to the United Nations, Fortune 500 companies, and the U.S. military.

Gregg is a member of scientific and visionary organizations, including the American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS), the Institute of HeartMath’s Global Coherence Initiative, and The Arlington Institute, as well as an original signatory of the 2017 Fuji Declaration, the international call to collectively catalyze a timely shift in the course of human history.

settings.title: Do I need a reservation with Gaia to visit Monument Valley?
settings.dropdown_text: Yes. While general visitors can access Monument Valley with a permit, this sacred journey with Gregg Braden requires an advance reservation due to the limited group size, private site access, and personalized itinerary. Early registration is encouraged to ensure your place on this once-in-a-lifetime experience.

settings.title: Do I need a tour guide at Monument Valley?
settings.dropdown_text: Absolutely, especially if you want to go beyond the surface. Monument Valley lies within Navajo Nation, and access to sacred areas like Mystery Valley, Big Hogan, and Tear Drop Arch is only permitted with a certified Navajo guide. This curated tour includes expert guides who offer cultural context, spiritual insight, and access to hidden locations unavailable to the general public.

settings.title: How many days do you need in Monument Valley?
settings.dropdown_text: While most travelers spend 1–2 days, this guided journey offers 10 days immersed in the land, allowing time to connect, reflect, and go beyond what a short visit can offer. Each day features teachings, sacred site visits, and meditations designed to deepen your experience, something a quick stop can’t begin to replicate.

settings.title: How many megalithic temples are in Malta?
settings.text: Malta is home to seven megalithic temple sites, recognized as UNESCO World Heritage Sites. These include Ġgantija, Ħaġar Qim, Mnajdra, Tarxien, Ta' Ħaġrat, Skorba, and Borg in-Nadur.

settings.title: What is the history behind the megalithic temples of Malta?
settings.text: Dating back to 3600–2500 BCE, Malta’s megalithic temples are among the oldest free-standing structures, predating the pyramids and Stonehenge. Built by a prehistoric civilization, they were used for religious and astronomical rituals. Their advanced architecture, including corbelled walls, altars, and carvings, showcases the engineering skills of Malta’s early builders.
